title: Rejoice, pray, give thanks (1 Thessalonians 5:12–24)
hookLine: rejoice evermore, pray without ceasing, in everything give thanks
tomorrow: a church full of busybodies. what's Paul's cure?

lines: THREE LINES ON A STICKY NOTE.
cards: Some weeks the worst day shows up right on schedule. The flight's canceled, the test comes back wrong, the rain starts the minute the boxes go outside, and everyone in the house is tired of everyone else.
Then somebody posts a verse about giving thanks in everything, and it lands like a slap. Does Paul really mean thank God for this?
Near the end of First Thessalonians, his sentences speed up, like someone at the door with a coat on, calling back the last important things. Three of them fit on a sticky note.

teach.b: The list starts with people: honor the ones who work hard among you, be at peace among yourselves, be patient toward everyone, and don't pay back evil for evil. Then the three.
Here they are: "Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you." Now read the third one slowly.

teach.h: IN EVERY THING, NOT FOR EVERY THING.
teach.b: In every thing. Not for every thing. Paul isn't asking anyone to be grateful for a diagnosis, a betrayal or a canceled flight.
He's saying that even inside it, there is something to thank God for. And remember who first heard this. In chapter one, this church received the word in much affliction.
Joy here isn't a mood that waits for good news.
Christians have read the middle line in different ways: a heart turned toward God all day, short prayers repeated through the hours, a life that never fully steps out of conversation with God.
Then a quick command: "Quench not the Spirit." And the last line turns everything around.

teach.h: FAITHFUL IS HE THAT CALLETH YOU.
teach.b: After all those orders, the weight lands somewhere else: "Faithful is he that calleth you, who also will do it."

how: Christians practice 'pray without ceasing' in different ways: short prayers repeated through the day, set times of prayer, or keeping a quiet awareness of God while working.

o: be glad in God, kept even on hard days
act cheerful so nobody worries about you
celebrate only when good news arrives

games.q: the sticky note — tap the pairs.

s: Paul says give thanks for every thing
the King James says in every thing give thanks: inside it, not for it.
the list ends with what God will do, not what the church must do
"Faithful is he that calleth you, who also will do it."
'pray without ceasing' has only ever been read one way
Christians read it as a heart turned to God all day, short repeated prayers, or an unbroken conversation.

games.q: a friend's dog died this morning. someone tells her 'everything happens for a reason, just be thankful.' what does 1 Thessalonians 5 actually say?
o: in every thing give thanks: not for the loss, but for something inside the day.
for every thing give thanks, including the loss itself.
give thanks only once the grief has fully passed.
games.why: the King James says in every thing, not for every thing. and Paul wrote it to a church that knew much affliction.

practice: Count three small things on your fingers that are good inside today, even if today is hard: a warm drink, a text back, one easy minute.

If you pray, the three can be your thanks; if not, just let each one land before you count the next. Small is fine. The point isn't to cover the hard thing over; it's to find what's still good while it's there.

wordCard.voice: Rejoice. Paul's first short command near the end of First Thessalonians: joy kept evermore, even in hard days, beside prayer and thanks.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: rejoice, pray, thank, and the last word belongs to the one who calls. See you tomorrow.
